title: Finance & Legal Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition (2028)
author: Emily Chen
summary: Operational playbook for Redwood Inference finance and legal teams covering budgeting & forecasting cadence, contracts lifecycle and approval matrix, procurement procedures and thresholds, and revenue recognition & billing policies (ASC 606 aligned). Intended for finance, legal, procurement, and business owners.
body:
Overview

Purpose
- Provide a single reference for finance and legal processes that materially affect forecasting, spend controls, vendor relationships, contract risk, and revenue recognition.
- Drive consistent decisions across hosted, dedicated, and private offerings.

Scope
- Applies to: FP&A, Legal, Procurement, Revenue Ops, Sales Finance, and Engineering teams when initiating spend, signing contracts, or recognizing revenue.
- Excludes payroll and benefits policies (see HR).

Key Contacts
- Finance (FP&A): Marcus Li (fpna@redwood.example.com)
- Legal: Priya Desai (legal@redwood.example.com)
- Procurement: Oliver Martinez (procurement@redwood.example.com)
- Revenue Ops / Billing: Nina Park (revenueops@redwood.example.com)

1) Budgeting & Forecasting\nOverview and cadence
- Annual budget (approved by Board in November) with quarterly re-forecasts.
- Rolling 12-month forecast updated monthly by FP&A; departmental owners update inputs on the 3rd business day.

Process and timeline (annual)
1. July: Budget kickoff — finance issues templates and assumptions.
2. August–September: Department submissions (headcount, opex, capex, projects).
3. October: Consolidation, scenario modeling (base / downside / upside).
4. November: Executive review and Board submission.
5. December: Budget finalized, control parameters published.

Forecast ownership and gates
- Department owners: accuracy of headcount and project timelines.
- FP&A: consolidation, sensitivity analysis, variance reporting.
- Finance Director (owner): final sign-off for monthly rolling forecast.

Templates and inputs
- Use the official budgeting template: BU-Budget-Template-v3.xlsx (located in Finance Drive). Key tabs: headcount, OPEX by vendor, capex, deferred revenue schedule.
- Required inputs each month: revenue by product line, pipeline conversion assumptions, deployment backlog for Dedicated & Private, projected model-serving cost (GPU hours).

Sustainability and controls
- Variance tolerance: +/- 3% monthly per department before mandatory review.
- Headcount freeze trigger: if trailing 3-month spend variance > 8% vs plan, hiring must be paused pending finance review.

2) Contracts & Legal Process\nContract lifecycle overview
- Request -> Drafting -> Review -> Risk Approval -> Signing -> CLM (storage) -> Execution tracking.

Requesting a contract
- All contract requests must be initiated via the Contract Intake form (Confluence link) and include: scope of work, counterparty details, estimated contract value, required term, data and security requirements, and billing terms.

Approval matrix (key thresholds)
- Contract Value < $50k: Legal review optional; FP&A notified.
- $50k - $250k: Legal review required; Finance director approval required.
- $250k - $1M: Legal sign-off + VP Finance approval.
- > $1M: Legal sign-off + CFO approval + Exec sponsor.
- Any contract with non-standard data residency, indemnity, or IP clauses must route to Legal regardless of value.

Standard clause guidance (examples)
- Term & termination: prefer 12-months rolling with 60-days termination notice for services.
- Liability cap: standard is aggregated fees paid in prior 12 months; exceptions require Legal approval.
- Data protection: include our standard DPA template for any customer data processing.

Contract management and storage
- Signed contracts must be uploaded to the CLM (Contractify) within 48 hours of signature and tagged with: customer, contract_owner, product_line, effective_date, renewal_date.
- CLM triggers automated renewal reminders to Legal and Account Owner 90/60/30 days before renewal.

Sample CLI snippet: upload signed contract via CLM API\ncurl -X POST https://clm.internal.api/contracts \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLM_TOKEN" \n  -F "file=@Signed-Agreement.pdf" \n  -F "metadata={\"customer\":\"Acme Corp\",\"contract_owner\":\"john.doe@redwood.example.com\"}"

3) Procurement Procedures

Purchase request flow
1. Initiate Purchase Request (PR) in Procurement Portal with justification, cost center, GL code, expected delivery date, and vendor.
2. Procurement validates vendor (KYC, tax forms, SLA review).
3. PO created and sent to vendor. Invoices must reference PO number.

Thresholds & approvals
- <$5k: Department head approval.
- $5k–$50k: Procurement + Department head.
- $50k–$250k: Procurement + Finance Director.
- >$250k: Procurement + VP Finance + Legal (contract required).

Vendor onboarding checklist
- W-9 or W-8 form (as applicable)
- Insurance certificate (if services > $50k)
- Security questionnaire (for vendors with data access)
- Signed Master Services Agreement (MSA) or PO terms

Competitive sourcing and exceptions
- Competitive bidding required for >$50k for non-strategic categories (3 vendor quotes minimum).
- Sole-source exceptions require written justification and VP Finance approval.

Sample PO JSON (for automated systems)
{
  "po_number": "PO-2026-01234",
  "vendor": "GPUCloud Inc.",
  "amount": "125000.00",
  "currency": "USD",
  "line_items": "See procurement system",
  "deliver_by": "2026-07-01"
}

Payment terms and invoice processing
- Standard terms: Net 30. Exceptions require Procurement + Finance approval.
- Invoices must include PO number and be sent to ap-invoices@redwood.example.com.
- Payment hold triggers: unresolved security or contract issues.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies

Accounting framework
- Redwood applies ASC 606 principles: identify contract, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price, and recognize revenue as performance obligations are satisfied.

Revenue triggers and common scenarios
- Hosted API usage: Recognize on a usage basis when invoiceable usage is measured (monthly).
- Dedicated capacity (reserved contracts): Recognize over time, ratably, over the contract term (subscription revenue) unless specific usage-based elements exist.
- Private deployments & on-prem: Recognize per contract terms and delivery milestones; software licenses recognized at transfer of control unless significant services are delivered separately.

Deferred revenue and invoices
- Payments received in advance must be recorded as deferred revenue until earned.
- Billing cadence: monthly for usage-based; upfront + monthly for mixed models; quarterly or annual invoicing only with Revenue Ops approval.

Credit notes and adjustments
- Credit memos require documented approval from Sales Finance and Revenue Ops.
- Material billing disputes (> $25k) must be escalated to VP Finance within 3 business days.

Sample revenue recognition rule (YAML snippet)
revenue_rule:
  product_line: "Redwood Dedicated"
  contract_type: "reserved"
  recognition: "ratable"
  allocate_basis: "time"
  deferred_account: "4100-DeferredRevenue"

Invoicing process and systems
- Primary billing system: Stripe for hosted customers (usage + invoices).
- AR ledger and revenue posting done in NetSuite.
- Integration checkpoints: daily usage export -> staging S3 -> ETL job -> Stripe/Netsuite sync.

Controls and SOX considerations
- Segregation of duties: billing, collections, and GL posting must be performed by separate roles.
- Monthly close checklist includes: reconciling deferred revenue ledger, unbilled receivables, and variance analysis for recognized revenue vs billings.

5) Exceptions, Non-standard Terms, and Escalation
- Any non-standard indemnity, data residency, or IP transfer clause requires Legal escalation.
- Pricing concessions > 20% off list price require Sales Finance sign-off.
- For procurement or contract exceptions, submit the Exception Request form with rationale, mitigations, and approver list.

6) Monitoring, Reporting, and KPIs
- Budget vs actual report cadence: monthly (FP&A distribution). Key metrics: burn rate, run-rate revenue, gross margin by product line.
- Procurement KPIs: PO cycle time, invoice exception rate, vendor on-time delivery.
- Revenue controls KPIs: % deferred revenue aging > 90 days, billing dispute volume, days sales outstanding (DSO).

Appendices
A. Sample approval email templates (contract, PO, credit memo)
B. Glossary of finance/legal terms used at Redwood
